content.en: Naresh, the 9-year-old son of Kamlesh, died on the 26th of November 1987 as a result of physical violence instigated by the police.

Kamlesh lives in a tiny, ill-lit single room in Delhi's Anand Parbat, a lower middle class colony. The room, along with many similar rooms which sur- round an open courtyard, and which have a single main entrance, is presently being disputed in court.

Anand Parbat, a colony which developed irregularly after Partition, has now become a very lucrative area for property developers, as it lies adjacent to large commercial and industrial areas. As a lot of money is involved, the local police, including the SHO Lal Singh, are involved in numerous illegal land deals.

As Kamlesh's husband is a long-haul truck driver Kamlesh stays alone in the room with her children, all minors. Kamlesh's actual landlord, who became missing during the November 1984 riots in Delhi, could not prove his ownership, and Kamlesh obtained a stay order from the court against eviction. Meanwhile, two men, claiming to be the new landlords, evicted the other residents of the building with the help of the local police.

The SHO, Lal Singh, kept harassing Kamlesh -- at times offering her Rs. 10,000 to leave the place, and at other times calling her unnecessarily to the police station and verbally abusing her. On the 13th of November, when Kamleshi was out, Lal Singh arrested her three children and kept them without food and water in the lock up the whole day. Ultimately, Kamlesh's lawyer's intervention was needed to get the children back.

On the evening of the 14th, Lal Singh (in mufti), with some other police and the two so-called landlords entered Kamlesh's room at 7.30 pm. and accused her of trespassing. Kamlesh was alone with her son Naresh. He started abusing and threatening her, and Naresh clung to her legs. Lal Singh then ordered the rest of the men in the room to kill the child to teach the mother a lesson, pulled the boy and flung him across the room, where the two landlords hit him repeatedly with bricks.

The police then dragged Kamlesh to the police station where they tore her clothes, and beat her some more. Lal Singh then took her to the Paharganj police station, where Kamlesh became unconscious. The police advised him to have an MLC done for her, but instead he brought her back to Anand Parbat, put her in the lock up, from where she was taken to Tihar Jail and then released two days later.

In the meantime, Kamlesh's children were taken in by a neighbour. When Kamlesh returned home, her son was seriously ill and local doctors advised hospitalization. Naresh was finally admitted into the Ram Manohar Lohia Hospital, where no MIC was automatically done, as the police there insisted that Lal Singh, when contacted, claimed there was no case for an MIC. Shortly Naresh went into a coma, from which he did not recover.

Kamlesh and her lawyer approached several police personnel, to have an MLC done for Naresh and to register a case against Lal Singh, Shambu Dayal and the others, but to no avail. Finally, on the 23rd, the ACP of Patel Nagar, within whose area Anand Parbat falls, agreed to come the next day, as he claimed to be extremely busy with VIP security that day. He however did find the time to go to the local doctors of Anand Parbat and to the neighbour who had taken in the children, and got statements from them that the injuries were not due to beating, and were more recent than the 14th. In the FIR which he made out for Kamlesh, he added the statement "the police did not beat my son. Shambu Dayal and his son were arrested on charges of attempted murder.

A late MLC was carried out on the 24th when Naresh was in a coma, which clearly underlined the injuries. However, the post mortem report, carried out at the police hospital, mentioned the cause of death as pneumonitis, and stated that the injuries had nothing to do with the death. Later when we spoke to some of the doctors who had attended to the child, we were told that pneumonitis was due to the injuries, and so the death of the child was clearly related to the beating.

Kamlesh, her husband, lawyer and some neigh- bours approached the Lt. Governor of Delhi for justice. After offering to transfer Lal Singh as a sop, the Lt. Governor instituted an SDM (Sub-divisional Magistrate) enquiry into the matter.

On the 5th of December, the vigilance branch of the Delhi police made out a confidential report where Lal Singh was implicated in the death, and where they clearly stated that the accused should not be released on bail as this would hinder the enquiry. Lal Singh was sent on leave, but returned before the enquiry was over. The charges against Shambu Dayal and his son were changed and they were released on bail, The SDM in charge of the enquiry who was very willing to listen to various witnesses, suddenly overnight became extre- mely secretive and refused to share his findings.

Since then, Shambu Dayal has cut off the electricity and water connections of Kamlesh's room: the latrine has been broken, and Kamlesh continues to be abused and threatened at all hours of the day and night. Lal Singh, who already has cases of assault and bribe against him at the Delhi High Court and who is out on bail at present, refuses to register any complaints made by Kamlesh, instead he has terrorized the neighbours and has forced them to file complaints against her.

Saheli took up Kamlesh's case and organized a meeting of various women's and civil rights groups. Together they demanded from the Lt. Governor that Lal Singh, Shambu Dayal and his son be arrested and that the findings of the SDM inquiry be made public. No action has been taken so far. The Commissioner of Police, Delhi, when contacted, has repeatedly adopted delaying tactics by suggesting that we get to the Crimes Against Women Cell, and from there to various departments none of whom is ready to say or do anything positive. Meanwhile Kamlesh continues to survive in this oppressive atmosphere, terrified of what may happen to her and her surviving children any time.

Kamlesh's case is yet another proof of women's extreme vulnerability in the face of police atrocities. Reports pouring in from all over the country of rapes by police only confirm this, and faced with the complicity within all levels of police and other law enforcement machinery, we are left with no choice but so take law into our own hands.
